title: Sky light: the design round for the pit, and which resolution to buy
question: Panel 2 is what I recommend building (0.13 ms/frame). Is it close enough to panel 1 to be worth it, or do you want the exact one at the cost of maintaining stored state?
context_md:
One test world holding every case at once — a 1-wide shaft, an 8-wide shaft, a 64-wide pit, a tunnel into a cliff, an overhanging lip, a sealed chamber. Dug parts cut **after** the surface freezes. Bright = sky light reaches here. Full report: `Reports/sky-light-design.md`.

**First finding: the light channel we already compute cannot do this**, and it is not tuning. It casts sun straight *down* a column and attenuates only through occluders, so a block-aligned **8-wide shaft reads 1.00 at 100 cells down** — your old "sunny sky all the way down" bug exactly. It also has a width threshold at exactly FIELD_SCALE (1-wide shaft dims, 8-wide does not), and it cuts rather than fades at a cave mouth (0.14 to 0.00 in five cells).

**Second finding: the fix is the seeding, not the propagation.** Seed sky light only where the cell is *outdoors* — the per-cell map that just shipped, which is the first bit of Terraria's wall layer — then spread with Terraria's own 0.91-per-air-cell, 0.56-per-solid decay. A shaft is not outdoors, so nothing is seeded in it and its light has to walk down from the mouth. Right on all seven geometries.

**Third finding: "Terraria does it per frame" does not transfer, because a Terraria tile is sixteen pixels.** Their screen light map is ~8,400 cells; ours per-pixel would be 163,840. So this has to run on a coarse grid. Swept:

| block | blocks | sweep | 1-wide shaft | tunnel mouth | pit rim |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| exact | 163,840 | 4.7 ms | 0.828 | 0.910 | 0.828 |
| 4 | 10,240 | **0.13 ms** | 0.245 | 0.770 | 0.725 |
| 8 (FIELD_SCALE) | 2,560 | 0.03 ms | 0.069 | 0.242 | 0.424 |

FIELD_SCALE's 8 is too coarse — the 1-wide shaft vanishes completely (panel 3), so it would fix the pit and leave shafts and tunnels looking exactly like today. Block size 4 is 10,240 blocks, which is almost exactly Terraria's screen map size; the prior art matches on grid size, not just algorithm.

One number worth noting: 0.91 per cell reaches a tenth in **24 cells**, and CAVE_FADE_DEPTH is 24 — set by eye here, independently.

items.label: 1 — exact, per pixel (the target look)
items.caption: Tapering wedges down both shafts, a gradient in the pit, a bright wedge into the tunnel, sealed chamber invisible. 4.7 ms per viewport — too slow per frame, fine as stored state.

meta.cost: 4.7 ms/viewport, or ~45 ms once at genesis

items.label: 2 — block size 4 (what I recommend)
items.caption: All three structures survive: both shafts, the pit gradient, the tunnel wedge. Dimmer than exact, and the 1-wide shaft most of all.

items.label: 3 — block size 8, our existing FIELD_SCALE (too coarse)
items.caption: The 1-wide shaft has vanished entirely and the tunnel is a nub. This is the version that would have shipped if I had reused FIELD_SCALE without measuring.
